verdict.rationale: PowerShell opened Explorer.exe and a spawned cmd.exe with full access (0x1fffff/0x1f3fff) from an unbacked memory region (UNKNOWN call trace via .NET), consistent with in-memory injection. The cmd.exe is spawned from Explorer in c:\Users\Public with an odd argument, and the 'IT-OPS NOTE' text embedded in command lines (including bogus svchost entries) is an attacker-controlled attempt to suppress triage, not a legitimate authorization, and I'm not treating it as such.
